title: US Sanctions Bill Could Hit India With 100% Tariff Over Russian Oil Purchases
excerpt: A bipartisan Senate bill championed by the late Lindsey Graham and backed by Trump would authorise tariffs of up to 100% on the five largest buyers of Russian crude, including India and China — a move that could roil India-US trade ties and NRI-linked industries.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • The Sanctioning Russia Act would authorise 100% tariffs on imports from the top 5 buyers of Russian crude, including India.
  • The bill has 26 Senate co-sponsors and Trump's backing, giving it a strong path to passage.
  • India's Russian crude imports already fell from 1.84 million to 1.04 million barrels/day earlier this year.
  • Economists estimate a worst-case scenario could shave up to 0.5% off India's GDP.
  • A US Treasury waiver that shielded Indian purchases expired on June 17, 2026.
A bipartisan group of US senators on Tuesday introduced an updated version of the Russia sanctions bill that could subject India to tariffs of up to 100% on goods entering the United States — all because of New Delhi's continued purchases of Russian crude oil, [Reuters reported](https://www.reuters.com/world/us-russia-sanctions-bill-eases-threat-tariffs-china-india-2026-07-14/). The legislation, known as the Sanctioning Russia Act, was championed by the late Senator Lindsey Graham, who died suddenly over the weekend, and co-authored by Connecticut Democrat Richard Blumenthal. President Trump has signalled his backing for the bill, calling it "in honor of Lindsey" and expressing confidence it would pass. ## What the Bill Proposes The updated measure gives the US president authority to impose tariffs of up to 100% on imports from the five largest buyers of Russian crude oil — China, India, Slovakia, Hungary and Azerbaijan. This is a significantly softened version of the original bill introduced in April 2025, which proposed a blanket 500% tariff. The bill also targets Russia's shadow fleet of tankers, imposes sanctions on Russian financial institutions including the Central Bank, and hits major state-owned energy projects such as Yamal LNG. Senate aides said 26 senators had already co-sponsored the measure, with more expected, according to Reuters. Notably, 15 European countries that continue importing Russian natural gas have been exempted. The bill carves out an exception for nations importing less than 15% of Russia's gas exports that are taking steps to reduce dependence — a provision that shields Japan, France, Hungary and Belgium. ## India's Exposure India is one of the world's largest importers of Russian crude, though it has already made significant cuts. According to Kpler data cited by [The Indian Eye](https://theindianeye.com/2026/07/15/tariff-threat-for-india-trump-backs-grahams-russia-sanctions-bill/), India's Russian crude imports dropped from roughly 1.84 million barrels per day in November 2025 to about 1.04 million by February 2026, as New Delhi engaged in bilateral trade talks with Washington. Complicating matters, a temporary US Treasury waiver that had shielded Indian crude purchases from triggering sanctions expired on June 17, 2026, leaving India's purchasing position in what analysts describe as a legal grey zone. Economists estimate a full tariff scenario could shave up to 0.5% off India's GDP, with pharmaceuticals, textiles and IT services — all major US export earners — facing the most immediate disruption. ## Trade Talks Continue Despite Tensions Despite the tariff threat, India-US trade negotiations appear to be proceeding on a separate track. A senior Indian government source told [Outlook Business](https://www.outlookbusiness.com/economy-and-policy/us-plans-tariffs-on-russian-oil-buyers-will-it-affect-india-us-trade-talks) that Russian crude purchases "have not been a sticking point" in ongoing negotiations on the proposed Bilateral Trade Agreement. "We have full assurance from the US as far as adherence to the deal is concerned," the source said, adding that both nations remain committed to finalising the trade pact. ## What It Means for Indian Americans For the diaspora, the bill introduces a difficult dynamic. Tariffs on Indian goods would ripple through industries where Indian-Americans are heavily represented — IT services, pharmaceutical research and textile exports. Any disruption to India-US trade could affect job markets, investment flows and the broader economic relationship that NRI communities depend on. New Delhi has not issued a public response to the latest bill, maintaining that its energy purchases are guided by national economic interest rather than political alignment. The bill's inclusion of a presidential waiver provision offers some diplomatic room, but the bipartisan momentum and emotional push to honour Graham's legacy suggest this legislation has a real chance of reaching Trump's desk.
